comparator.name: Classics (Greek and Latin Language and Culture)
comparator.academicYear: Indicative prospective-student curriculum: year 1 labelled 2027–2028, years 2 and 3 labelled 2028–2029
comparator.sourceNotes: The official prospectus shows 60 EC in each year. Year 1 comprises twelve compulsory 5-EC courses; the 0-EC mentoring and academic-writing activities and the optional 5-EC language intensification for entrants without a school examination in Greek or Latin are excluded. Year 2 combines six required 5-EC courses with two restricted-choice Humanities minors (15 EC each). The domestic year-three route has four required 5-EC courses, a 10-EC Classics bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuinely free elective space. Its 5-EC personal-development completion remains a separate required credit-bearing component. The year pages are indicative and carry inconsistent prospective labels rather than an established single cohort's guaranteed timetable.

programmes.label: Classics (Greek and Latin Language and Culture) at Radboud University

exception.reason: The Greek and Latin grammar, translation, linguistics and original-text literature sequence is integral to Classics across all three years. UCR offers Greek archaeology, ancient democracy and world mythology, but no ancient Greek or Latin language teaching or sustained primary-text sequence. A 24-course UCR programme built around adjacent cultural-history courses would conceal this defining gap rather than constitute a defensible closest match.
exception.curriculumContext: Radboud's prospective-student year pages are explicitly indicative and have different projected year labels; the 180-EC reconstruction combines their published domestic route and does not claim a guaranteed Fall 2026-entry timetable. Restricted year-two minors and the open year-three elective space remain explicit.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 course rows in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including names, outlines/profiles, topics, methods, planned semesters and prerequisites. MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature and MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology address portions of ancient material culture and literary themes. No Greek or Latin grammar, translation, original-language text, classical philology or sustained Classics language sequence is available, so these complementary courses cannot anchor a defensible 24-course closest-match programme.
